clue.text: Excellent performer in school play?

parts.note: a class is a group of pupils taught together in a school
an act is a section of a play, or a turn on stage

explanation.surface: Someone shines in the school drama production.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'school play' is not a nativity show but two separate pieces put side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic: a first-rate person, especially an impressive entertainer, is called a class act.

clue.text: Oddly, collie chewed half a chestnut

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the dog word
half takes the opening three of the six letters of chewed

explanation.surface: A dog gnawed through half of a conker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnut' looks like the nut; it is the old chestnut, a stale joke or saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An old chestnut is a joke or phrase repeated so often it is stale, a hackneyed remark.

clue.text: Records Pavlova leftovers being emptied out

parts.note: Anna Pavlova was the famous Russian ballerina

indicators.note: emptied out removes all the inside letters of leftovers, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: The remains of a pavlova dessert are scraped from the plates.
explanation.walkthrough: Pavlova looks like the meringue dessert, but it is the dancer, giving her first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Annals are historical records kept year by year, a synonym for chronicles.

clue.text: Absolutely right, argued the anguished

parts.note: so as an intensifier means absolutely, as in so true
rowed, rhyming with cowed, means quarrelled or argued

explanation.surface: Someone in distress argues that they are entirely correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowed here means quarrelled, not pulled oars.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are past-tense verbs meaning felt grief or deep distress.

clue.text: Dictator in corner at folk dancing

indicators.note: dancing jumbles the letters as dancers move around, here the three words corner at folk

explanation.surface: A tyrant tucked in a corner at a folk dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' looks political; it means a bossy person who must control everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose synonym: a person who insists on dictating how everything is done, domineering in private life.

clue.text: Kind of iron age bird

parts.note: pig iron is crude iron straight from the blast furnace
an eon is an immensely long age

explanation.surface: Sounds like a description of a bird from the Iron Age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron age' reads as the prehistoric period, but the words split: 'Kind of iron' and then 'age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple synonym: the common town bird, a dove relative found in every city square.

clue.text: Princess's confession of drug-dealing

definitions.meaning: the Irish princess of the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera
split as ..., an admission of selling ecstasy, E being slang for that drug

explanation.surface: A royal admits she has been selling narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess loved by Tristan in the medieval romance and Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Engineered, and hence improved

indicators.note: engineered means constructed or contrived, so the letters of and hence are reassembled

explanation.surface: Something was engineered and therefore got better.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something enhanced has been made better or increased in quality.

clue.text: Heard naked girl in capital city

indicators.note: heard says the phrase is spoken and the entry is what it sounds like

parts.note: naked means nude, unclothed; Ellie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone heard that an unclothed woman was in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: New Delhi is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Uneducated Italian woman rejected at first, not disheartened

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for the woman is thrown away

parts.note: signora is the Italian title for a married woman

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the little word goes

parts.note: taken as written before losing its middle

explanation.surface: An Italian lady, rebuffed at the outset, is unschooled but not discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected at first' drops S from SIGNORA leaving IGNORA; 'disheartened' removes O from NOT leaving NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking knowledge or schooling, uninformed.

clue.text: Someone who doesn't turn up as meal currently doesn't have starter

parts.note: nosh is British slang for food or a meal

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for currently is missing

parts.note: now means at present, currently

explanation.surface: A guest who fails to appear for dinner and so misses the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't have starter' takes N off NOW, giving OW; 'starter' teasingly suggests a first course of the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is the standard term for a person who books or is expected and never arrives.

clue.text: A rush to acquire drug which gives heavenly bodies

indicators.note: the phrase a rush takes in the drug, so it goes inside

parts.note: to belt is to rush or race at speed
a steroid is a type of drug, such as an anabolic steroid

explanation.surface: An athlete hurries to get performance drugs to build a heavenly physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to acquire' is the containment signal: the opening phrase takes the drug inside it. 'Rush' as a verb is the slang sense of belting along.
explanation.definitionFit: The asteroid belt is the region between Mars and Jupiter full of orbiting rocky bodies.

clue.text: Derelict cell refashioned as multiple occupancy accommodation

indicators.note: derelict means ruined and fallen apart, so the following letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A run-down prison cell has been converted into shared housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refashioned' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'Derelict' rearranges CELL REFASHIONED.
explanation.definitionFit: A university building where many students live together is a shared residential block of this name.

clue.text: I say, that is small footwear

parts.note: well is an exclamation of surprise, like I say
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: An exclamation at how tiny some shoes are.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellies is the British colloquial name for wellington boots, rubber waterproof boots.

clue.text: Get engaged in game show

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words game show, across their join

explanation.surface: Someone becomes betrothed on a television quiz programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get engaged' suggests a marriage proposal; here it is the mechanical sense of gears engaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear teeth mesh when they interlock, that is, become engaged with each other.

clue.text: The result of one's girlfriends meeting gradually

definitions.text: The result of one's girlfriends meeting
definitions.meaning: a bit is slang for a girlfriend, so one bit beside another bit
little by little, a step at a time

explanation.surface: Two partners finally meet, and things develop slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: Bit is dated British slang for a young woman or girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: slowly, in small stages, one small piece after another.

clue.text: Members of GMB lack legitimacy for one refusing to strike

indicators.note: Members of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Union members complain that the GMB lacks legitimacy in a strike dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: GMB is a large British trade union, which fits the strike theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackleg is a derogatory term for a worker who carries on working during a strike, a scab.

clue.text: Scoff at ball girl entertaining heads of international tennis tournament

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the head letters go inside

parts.note: the belle of the ball is the prettiest girl there

indicators.note: heads of takes the opening letter of each of the three following words

explanation.surface: A ball girl at a big tennis event hosts the sport's leaders, who mock her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball girl' suggests tennis courts, but it is the belle at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to belittle is to disparage or make light of, as scoffing does.

clue.text: Regularly indulged in lounge

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word indulged, from the first

explanation.surface: Someone who has often indulged themselves in a lounge bar.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to lounge is to laze about doing nothing, a synonym.

clue.text: Public official's first love is moving east to become singer

indicators.note: in an across entry east is rightwards, so that letter shifts one place further along

parts.note: a coroner is the official who investigates sudden deaths
love is zero in tennis, the letter O; first picks the first of the two O letters

explanation.surface: A council officer's first romance makes them head east to become a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: The first O in CORONER moves right past the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner is a singer of sentimental ballads in a soft style, like Bing Crosby.

clue.text: Arrange official document, being penniless

indicators.note: penniless removes every P, the abbreviation for penny

parts.note: a passport is an official travel document

explanation.surface: Someone without money sorts out their official papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Both P letters go, as P stands for penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to arrange or sort into groups.

clue.text: Stop time

definitions.meaning: the US word for a full stop at the end of a sentence
a span or era of time

explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a full stop by this name, and it also means a length of time.

clue.text: Rise up like church leaders in 8

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
CE is the Church of England
the leading letters of the two words of the answer at 8 down, the Indian capital

explanation.surface: Church leaders in India's capital climb upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to 8-down, NEW DELHI, whose initials are N and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ascend is to climb or go upward.

clue.text: Brake discs avert disaster, but passengers in critical condition

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, so the letters of the first three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Good brakes prevent a crash, but the people riding along are badly hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'critical condition' looks medical; it means the passengers are critical, criticising the driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Back-seat drivers are passengers who keep criticising and directing the person at the wheel.

clue.text: Large wave of misfortune in part of Hull

indicators.note: in places the misfortune word inside the hull part

parts.note: the bow is the front part of a ship's hull
ill as a noun means harm or misfortune

explanation.surface: A huge wave of bad luck strikes a district of Hull, the English port city.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Hull look like the Yorkshire city, but it is a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a great swelling wave of the sea.

clue.text: Straddle Alton Towers' star attraction?

definitions.meaning: to sit or stand with one leg each side of something
read as two words, the finest ride at the theme park; Alton Towers is a big English theme park with roller coasters

explanation.surface: Climbing astride the headline ride at a theme park.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second reading splits the word into two.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride something is to sit or stand astride it, legs either side.

clue.text: This evening, son's working out in pantihose

indicators.note: out says the word for working is taken away from the evening word

parts.note: tonight means this evening
on means working or operating, as a machine is on
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Tonight a son is exercising while wearing hosiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working out' looks like exercise; it is ON (working) taken out of TONIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pantihose (pantyhose) are sheer leg-and-waist garments, the same as women's hosiery.

clue.text: Was among the spectators perhaps as a race finished

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
ended means finished

explanation.surface: Someone watched in the crowd as a race came to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks being a spectator as one example of attending.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to be present at an event, and spectators are one sort of people present.
